recipes.name: Best Ziti Ever with Sausage
ingredients_raw: 1 pound mild Italian sausage, casings removed
2 (24 ounce) jars Classico® Tomato and Basil Sauce

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.

Place sausage in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble and set aside. In a large saucepan, heat pasta sauce with 1 teaspoon basil until bubbling. In a medium bowl, mix together ricotta, 1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, salt and pepper.

Spread bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish with sauce. Layer 1/2 of the ziti, 1/2, the sausage, 1/2 of the ricotta, and 1/2 the mozzarella. Spoon half of the sauce over top. Repeat layers. Sprinkle top with remaining 1/2 teaspoons basil and Italian seasoning.
Bake in preheated oven for 40 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Best Ziti Ever with Sausage
raw_recipe.description: Ziti is layered with sausage, ricotta, mozzarella and tomato sauce, then baked until bubbling.

review.reviewBody: I made this using ground turkey instead of sausage to cut down a little on fat. I also made my own tomato sauce, and added some parmesan and an egg to the ricotta, then layered the whole thing like you would lasagna. I really liked the ease of assembly, versus lasagna which takes forever. I froze part of it for later, and it froze wonderfully. Such a good, easy casserole that can be made ahead of time. I adjusted seasonings a lot to suit our tastes, and used fresh garlic and onion, but the idea was the same. Thanks!

I rarely make a recipe twice, but I've made this one three times now. It's always a hit. I've added some grated zucchini in with the meat mixture, to add some more veggies. No one noticed, but I got to feel like it was a bit healthier!
I made a half recipe in an 8x8. Very good. Next time maybe a little more sauce and switch the top layers of sauce and cheese so the mozzarella is on top.

I did not change much in the way of ingredients. My changes were in the way it was put together. I mixed the sour cream with the noodles. I mixed the meat in the sauce. I did not have provolone so used mozzarella and Parmesan. I will make this again and try it with the provolone. My family loved it.

I used 2 lbs of Italian sausage, one hot, one mild. I used 1 1/2 jars of sauce (36 oz). I added one egg to the ricotta mixture (I used all 15 oz from the container.) The consistency and moisture was great. Flavor was dissappointely salty and I did not add any salt! I will need to check salt content on each ingredient next time.

Very good and easy recipe!. I used gluten free pasta, Low Fodmap spaghetti sauce and ground beef instead of sausage since I avoid onion and garlic seasoning and it really turned out fabulous! Highly recommend!

This was so good. I adjusted the servings to 6, so we would have leftovers. I got 4 meals out of it & Kraig got 3! 
I added died tomatoes, 1 can of mushrooms, and half a bag of frozen peas. I started doing the layering but then when i got to the end and realized i needed to open up that second jar of pasta sauce and poured it on top, i kind of stirred everything up. it doesn't stay in a layer anyways so that's kind of pointless. I also substituted cottage cheese for ricotta cheese - which we like better anyways, plus it's healthier!

This....was awesome. Tasted close to lasagna, and better than some lasagna's I've had lol. Pretty to make. I used cottage cheese because it was cheaper, and it still turned out great. Will be making it again. To try and make it a little healthier I used ground turkey and seasoned it heavily like a sausage is and it did the job great.

YES! So yummy. Make it!
Few changes I made: Add chopped onion, garlic and green pepper to the (hot italian) sausage when browning. Also used fresh basil in the sauce instead of dried. That's it.
So freakin' good, I will definitely make this again - in place of boring old pasta and sauce.
I added one pound of Italian sausage and one pound of beef, but otherwise stayed with the recipe and it was awesome! My husband doesn’t like pasta but he liked this!

This was the first time I've ever cooked ziti and I'll say it was farely easy. This recipe was good, the only thing I changed was that I added half sausage half ground beef. Also while browing the meat, I added garlic, onion and green bell peppers. Tasty
Used penne noodles instead of ziti because that's what I had... but turned out fantastic! The kids loved it
I thought it was good. The only thing different I would do is add more sausage, and maybe some fresh grated Parmesan on top with fresh parsley.

Easy weeknight recipe, but feel the ingredients could come together better perhaps with some eggs. I'd also consider trying this with onion sautéed in with the sausage. As is, this makes a huge portion that could easily stretch to 10-12 servings.
Easy and delicious. Next time I’ll heat up some extra sauce to juice it up a bit
Perfect recipe for an easy weeknight meal. Replaced sausage with shredded chicken and cut the richotta in half to make it a little lighter.
Yes I had ground beef, instead of sausage and it is delicious. Thanks
I made this not changing anything, wanted to see what original flavor was. It was great!. Just moved out of NY and I miss my Italian food. It was so good, had it 2 days in a row. Thank you!
This is fairly easy to put together, and it's pretty tasty, but improvements can be made.
This was delicious and I plan on putting it into my regular rotation. It’s so simple and easily customizable- the sign of a great recipe!
